title: “SPEAK, LORD.”
paragraphs:
But the night they were whispered…
a sleeping nation began to wake.
The lamp of God was still burning in the tabernacle.

The priests were corrupt.
The people were drifting.
And the voice of God had grown… rare.
Then heaven chose the most unlikely listener.

Not a prophet.
Not a king.

Still young. Still learning.
Sleeping near the Ark where the presence of God dwelt.
A voice cut through the darkness.
Until the old priest finally understood something terrifying… and beautiful.
And the child didn’t yet know His voice.
So Eli whispered instructions that would echo through history:
‘Speak, LORD, for Your servant is listening.’”
This time the boy didn’t run.
And heaven entrusted a child with a message that would reshape a nation.
Because revival doesn’t always start in palaces.
Sometimes it begins in the quiet obedience of a young heart willing to listen.
Here’s the truth many of us forget:
God still calls names in the night.
Sometimes with a whisper inside the soul.
But most people never hear it…
Samuel heard because he was available.
Because he stayed near the presence of God.
Because when the moment came… he surrendered.
And the Gospel reminds us why this still matters.
Centuries later, another voice would call ordinary people by name.
And the world was never the same.

Because the God who called Samuel in the night
is the same God who still calls hearts today.

Through His Word.
Through His Spirit.
Through the voice of Jesus Christ.
The question isn’t whether God still speaks.
Tonight, maybe your prayer is simple.
And if you’ve wandered far, remember this:

The same Jesus who calls you
also died and rose again to bring you home.

Because one listening heart
can still change a nation.
We tell the stories that shame tried to erase.
